stem: A charge nurse is determining the appropriate RN, LPN/LVN, and assistive-personnel mix for a shift. Which factors should drive the staffing decision?

options.A: Base the staffing mix primarily on staff seniority and address competency differences after assignments are made.
options.B: Use the same staffing pattern throughout the shift even when patient acuity, workload, and required competencies change.
options.C: Base assignments primarily on staff scheduling preferences once the planned head count has been met.
options.D: Base the staffing mix on patient care needs, acuity, and workload, matched with each staff member's authorized scope or role, education, skills, competencies, experience, and relevant unit/support factors.

rationale: ANA staffing principles state that appropriate staffing is driven by the needs of the healthcare consumer or population and must account for patient acuity/intensity, workload, required clinical competencies, staff education, skill mix, experience, scope of practice, and characteristics/resources of the practice environment. Staffing plans must also be flexible enough to respond to changes in patient needs and care demands across and within shifts. Therefore D is correct. Seniority alone, a fixed staffing pattern, or scheduling preferences/head count alone do not address the patient- and competency-based factors required for safe staffing.
educational_objective: Build a safe nursing skill mix by matching changing patient needs, acuity and workload with the authorized scope, competence, education, experience and available support of the nursing team rather than relying on head count, seniority or preference alone.
source_document_title: Principles for Nurse Staffing, 3rd Edition; Workforce Management
source_version_date: ANA Principles for Nurse Staffing, 3rd Edition (2019) with current ANA staffing guidance live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: ANA Principles for Nurse Staffing: staffing decisions are based on the number and needs of healthcare consumers/populations; population needs determine required competencies; staff should practice to license/education/scope/documented competence; staffing plans adjust to changes in care needs across hours/shifts/days. ANA Workforce Management: staffing resources consider patient care needs/acuity/intensity/workload together with staff skill mix, education, competencies, experience, unit variables and available resources.
source_claim_supported: Safe staffing and skill-mix decisions are dynamic and should match patient needs, acuity and workload with staff scope, education, skills, competencies, experience and relevant unit/resource factors rather than relying on seniority, preferences or fixed head count alone.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care > Assignment, Delegation and Supervision: identify assignments based on client needs; assign/delegate to personnel with appropriate competency and within allowable duties; evaluate staff ability considering competency, judgment and decision-making; establish priorities based on acuity.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — staffing skill mix, assignment, competency and acuity

source_original.stem: A charge nurse is determining the appropriate RN, LPN/LVN, and assistive-personnel mix for a shift. Which factors should drive the staffing decision?

options.A: Base the staffing mix primarily on staff seniority because competency differences are addressed after assignments are made.
options.B: Use the same staffing pattern throughout the shift even when patient acuity and required competencies change.
options.C: Base assignments primarily on staff scheduling preferences when the planned head count has been met.
options.D: Base the staffing mix on patient care needs and acuity together with staff scope, education, skills, competencies, and relevant unit factors.

source_original.rationale: ANA staffing principles emphasize matching staffing resources to patient needs and considering patient acuity, skill mix, education, competencies, unit variables, and changing care demands. A fixed or seniority-only approach does not address safe staffing requirements.
source_original.source_detail: Staffing decisions incorporate patient needs, acuity, competencies, skill mix, and practice-setting factors Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: prioritization, assignment/delegation, advocacy/client rights, continuity/referral, legal scope, professional limitations and emergency/quality-management activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the staffing-skill-mix construct and key D, expanded the keyed factors to include workload, authorized scope/role, experience and support resources, strengthened the dynamic-acuity requirement, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests a defined safe-staffing principle rather than a complex calculation.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Safe staffing and nursing skill mix
audit_findings.source_authority: Current ANA staffing principles/workforce guidance with NCSBN 2026 blueprint alignment
audit_findings.currentness: ANA current staffing pages live-rechecked 2026-08-16; 3rd-edition staffing principles remain the active ANA framework
audit_findings.exact_locator: ANA Principles for Nurse Staffing current page and Workforce Management staffing factors; NCSBN Management of Care assignment/delegation/acuity statements
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses patient-needs/acuity/workload and staff-scope/competency/resource factors supported by ANA and does not claim a universal fixed RN:LPN:UAP ratio or jurisdiction-independent scope for LPN/LVN/UAP roles.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because seniority alone does not establish required competence or safe patient assignment.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because staffing must adapt to changes in acuity, workload and required competencies.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because preference and head count alone do not ensure appropriate skill mix or competency matching.
distractor_audit.D: Correct and directly ANA-supported while preserving jurisdiction-specific scope/role boundaries.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only D combines patient demand, workload and staff scope/competency/resource factors without substituting a single administrative variable for clinical staffing judgment.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are staffing-decision frameworks; the key is determined by the complete patient/competency model rather than wording length alone.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care — staffing, assignment, competency and acuity-based resource allocation.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current ANA staffing principles and workforce-management guidance, all options, rationale, objective, scope-of-practice caveat, difficulty, ambiguity, cueing and NCSBN Management of Care alignment. D remained uniquely correct.
